b1-01.title: Offices and documents: codice fiscale, residence, permit

steps.title: Saying what you need
steps.how_to: How to say what you need and what you have to do at an office.
steps.intro: At an Italian office you'll hear bisogna for what you have to do and serve or servono for what you need. You can use them yourself to ask what to bring.

examples.said: Bisogna prendere il numero.
examples.en: You have to take a ticket.

examples.said: Serve una marca da bollo da sedici euro.
examples.en: You need a sixteen-euro revenue stamp.

examples.said: Servono due fototessere.
examples.en: You need two passport photos.

examples.said: Bisogna prendere l'appuntamento online?
examples.en: Do you have to book the appointment online?

steps.notice: Bisogna is followed by a verb and never changes; serve and servono are followed by the thing you need, servono for more than one, because the thing is what's needed.
steps.context: Italian offices often want an appointment booked online and a marca da bollo bought beforehand at a tabaccheria.

ask.said: Sei all'anagrafe e c'è la fila. Cosa fai prima?
ask.en: You're at the registry office and there's a line. What do you do first?

answer.said: Prima bisogna prendere il numero.
answer.en: First you have to take a ticket.

ask.said: Cosa porti in comune per la residenza?
ask.en: What do you bring to city hall to register your residence?

answer.said: Servono il passaporto e il contratto d'affitto.
answer.en: You need your passport and your lease.

ask.said: Per il permesso di soggiorno, cosa porti in questura?
ask.en: For your residence permit, what do you bring to the questura?

answer.said: Servono la ricevuta e quattro fototessere.
answer.en: You need the receipt and four passport photos.

mission.goal: Ask what you need to register your residence.

say.said: Buongiorno, devo richiedere la residenza. Cosa serve?
say.en: Good morning, I need to register my residence. What do I need?

steps.title: Checking what's enough
steps.how_to: How to ask whether something is enough with basta.
steps.intro: Basta means that something is enough, or that all you have to do is one thing. It's how you check with a clerk whether a copy will do.

examples.said: Per il contratto basta la fotocopia?
examples.en: For the lease, is a photocopy enough?

examples.said: Sì, basta la fotocopia.
examples.en: Yes, a photocopy is enough.

examples.said: Basta firmare qui.
examples.en: You just need to sign here.

examples.said: Bastano due righe.
examples.en: Two lines are enough.

steps.notice: Basta plus a thing means that thing is enough, and basta plus a verb means that's all you have to do; with more than one thing it's bastano, because it matches what's enough.
steps.context: Italian offices usually ask for the original and a photocopy of every document.

ask.said: Hai solo la fotocopia del contratto. Cosa chiedi all'impiegata?
ask.en: You only have a photocopy of your lease. What do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Basta la fotocopia?
answer.en: Is a photocopy enough?

ask.said: Hai perso l'autocertificazione. Cosa devi fare?
ask.en: You lost your self-certification form. What do you have to do?

answer.said: Basta compilare di nuovo il modulo.
answer.en: I just have to fill out the form again.

ask.said: Il tuo amico vuole portare dieci fototessere. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: Your friend wants to bring ten passport photos. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Bastano quattro fototessere.
answer.en: Four passport photos are enough.

mission.goal: Ask whether a photocopy of your lease is enough.

say.said: Per il contratto basta la fotocopia?
say.en: For the lease, is a photocopy enough?

steps.title: Asking how long it takes
steps.how_to: How to ask and say how long something takes with ci vuole and ci vogliono.
steps.intro: Ci vuole and ci vogliono say how long something takes. You'll use them to ask about any application or permit.

examples.said: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
examples.en: How long does it take?

examples.said: Ci vuole un mese.
examples.en: It takes a month.

examples.said: Ci vogliono alcune settimane.
examples.en: It takes a few weeks.

examples.said: E quanto tempo ci vuole per avere il permesso nuovo?
examples.en: And how long does it take to get the new permit?

steps.notice: Ci vuole goes with one thing or amount and ci vogliono with more than one, because it agrees with the time it takes.

ask.said: Vuoi sapere quando è pronta la tua pratica. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You want to know when your application will be ready. What do you ask?

answer.said: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
answer.en: How long does it take?

ask.said: Il permesso nuovo è pronto domani?
ask.en: Is the new permit ready tomorrow?

answer.said: No, ci vogliono alcune settimane.
answer.en: No, it takes a few weeks.

ask.said: Per la residenza, quanto aspetti di solito?
ask.en: For residence registration, how long do you usually wait?

answer.said: Di solito ci vogliono quarantacinque giorni.
answer.en: It usually takes forty-five days.

mission.goal: Ask how long your application will take.

say.said: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
say.en: How long does it take?

steps.title: Following a clerk's instructions
steps.how_to: How to understand the polite instructions a clerk gives you.
steps.intro: Clerks give instructions with the polite command form. Once you know the endings, you can follow them without asking for English.

examples.said: Compili il modulo.
examples.en: Fill out the form.

examples.said: Firmi qui in fondo.
examples.en: Sign here at the bottom.

examples.said: Prenda il numero e aspetti.
examples.en: Take a ticket and wait.

examples.said: Torni con la ricevuta fra trenta giorni.
examples.en: Come back with the receipt in thirty days.

steps.notice: A polite instruction ends in -i for -are verbs and in -a for -ere and -ire verbs, so firmi means "sign," not "you sign."

ask.said: Cosa ti dice l'impiegata quando ti dà il modulo?
ask.en: What does the clerk tell you when she hands you the form?

answer.said: Compili il modulo e firmi qui in fondo.
answer.en: Fill out the form and sign here at the bottom.

ask.said: All'anagrafe c'è la fila. Cosa ti dice l'impiegato?
ask.en: There's a line at the registry office. What does the clerk tell you?

answer.said: Prenda il numero e aspetti.
answer.en: Take a ticket and wait.

ask.said: La tua pratica non è finita. Cosa ti dice l'impiegato?
ask.en: Your application isn't done yet. What does the clerk tell you?

answer.said: Torni con la ricevuta fra trenta giorni.
answer.en: Come back with the receipt in thirty days.

mission.goal: Ask the clerk what to do next and follow the instructions.

say.said: Mi scusi, cosa devo fare adesso?
say.en: Excuse me, what do I do now?

steps.title: Asking which and how come
steps.how_to: How to ask which one, how come and how far along.
steps.intro: Quale, come mai and a che punto let you ask exactly what you need at an office. You'll use them at the counter and on the phone.

examples.said: Quale modulo devo compilare?
examples.en: Which form do I need to fill out?

examples.said: Quali documenti servono?
examples.en: Which documents do I need?

examples.said: Buongiorno, chiamo per sapere a che punto è la mia pratica.
examples.en: Good morning, I'm calling to find out where my application stands.

examples.said: Come mai ci vuole così tanto?
examples.en: How come it's taking so long?

steps.notice: Quale picks one from a set and quali more than one, because it agrees; come mai asks "how come," and a che punto asks how far along something is.

ask.said: Ci sono tre moduli sul tavolo. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: There are three forms on the table. What do you ask?

answer.said: Quale modulo devo compilare?
answer.en: Which form do I need to fill out?

ask.said: Aspetti la tua pratica da due mesi. Cosa chiedi al telefono?
ask.en: You've been waiting on your application for two months. What do you ask on the phone?

answer.said: Buongiorno, a che punto è la mia pratica?
answer.en: Good morning, where does my application stand?

ask.said: Al telefono ti dicono che manca un documento. Come rispondi?
ask.en: On the phone they tell you a document is missing. How do you answer?

answer.said: Come mai? L'ho consegnato a maggio!
answer.en: How come? I turned it in in May!

mission.goal: Ask how far along your application is.

say.said: Buongiorno, a che punto è la mia pratica?
say.en: Good morning, where does my application stand?

b1-02.title: Doing things for people: combined pronouns

steps.title: Bringing it to you
steps.how_to: How to say "it to me" and "it to you" with me lo, te la and the rest.
steps.intro: Two small words together, like me lo or te la, say "it to me" or "it to you." You'll use them to offer, lend and ask for things without naming them again.

examples.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
examples.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

examples.said: Sì, scusa! Te la porto subito.
examples.en: Yes, sorry! I'll bring it right over.

examples.said: Se ti serve il trapano, te lo presto volentieri.
examples.en: If you need the drill, I'm happy to lend it to you.

examples.said: Le chiavi? Te le restituisco stasera.
examples.en: The keys? I'll give them back to you tonight.

steps.notice: The "to whom" word comes first and mi or ti become me or te, then lo, la, li or le for the thing, because it matches the thing: la for the ladder, le for the keys.
steps.context: In almost any shop you can say "È un regalo" and they'll gift-wrap it for free.

ask.said: Un amico ti chiede i tuoi libri. Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: A friend asks to borrow your books. What do you say?

answer.said: Te li presto volentieri.
answer.en: I'm happy to lend them to you.

ask.said: La tua vicina vuole indietro la sua scala. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: Your neighbor wants her ladder back. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Te la porto subito.
answer.en: I'll bring it right over.

ask.said: Compri un libro per un'amica. Cosa chiedi al libraio?
ask.en: You're buying a book for a friend. What do you ask the bookseller?

answer.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
answer.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

mission.goal: Ask the shopkeeper to gift-wrap what you bought.

say.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
say.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

steps.title: Doing it for someone else
steps.how_to: How to say "it to him," "it to her" or "it to you" with glielo.
steps.intro: Glielo says "it to him," "it to her," or "it to you" when you're being polite. You'll hear it in every shop and use it to pass things on.

examples.said: Glielo dico io.
examples.en: I'll tell him.

examples.said: Gliela incarto subito.
examples.en: I'll wrap it for you right away.

examples.said: Glielo taglio sottile come prima?
examples.en: Should I slice it thin for you, like before?

examples.said: Sì, glielo scrivo qui.
examples.en: Sure, I'll write it down for you here.

steps.notice: Gli, le and Le all become glie- and join lo, la, li or le as one word, so the same glielo means to him, to her or to you; the situation tells you who.

ask.said: Il libraio ti chiede il numero di telefono. Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: The bookseller asks for your phone number. What do you say?

answer.said: Sì, glielo scrivo qui.
answer.en: Sure, I'll write it down for you here.

ask.said: Marco non sa niente della festa. Cosa dici agli amici?
ask.en: Marco doesn't know anything about the party. What do you tell your friends?

answer.said: Glielo dico io.
answer.en: I'll tell him.

ask.said: Lavori in un negozio e una signora compra un regalo. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: You work in a shop and a woman buys a gift. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Glielo incarto subito.
answer.en: I'll wrap it for you right away.

mission.goal: Offer to pass a message on to someone.

say.said: Non ti preoccupare, glielo dico io.
say.en: Don't worry, I'll tell him.

steps.title: Asking for a bit more
steps.how_to: How to ask for some more of something with me ne.
steps.intro: Me ne dà means "could you give me some" or "could you give me two." It's what you say at the deli counter when you want more.

examples.said: È buonissimo. Me ne dà ancora un etto?
examples.en: It's delicious. Could I have another hundred grams?

examples.said: Me ne dà un pezzetto da assaggiare?
examples.en: Could I have a little piece to taste?

examples.said: Me ne dà due, per favore.
examples.en: Could I have two, please?

examples.said: Te ne porto due.
examples.en: I'll bring you two.

steps.notice: Ne means "of it" or "of them" and joins like lo, so mi becomes me: me ne dà due; with an amount, ne is always there, because the amount is of something.

ask.said: Il prosciutto è buonissimo. Cosa chiedi al salumiere?
ask.en: The prosciutto is delicious. What do you ask the deli man?

answer.said: Me ne dà ancora un etto?
answer.en: Could I have another hundred grams?

ask.said: Vuoi assaggiare il pecorino. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You want to taste the pecorino. What do you ask?

answer.said: Me ne dà un pezzetto da assaggiare?
answer.en: Could I have a little piece to taste?

ask.said: Un amico non ha bicchieri per la festa. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend doesn't have glasses for the party. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Te ne porto due.
answer.en: I'll bring you two.

mission.goal: Ask for another hundred grams at the deli counter.

say.said: Me ne dà ancora un etto?
say.en: Could I have another hundred grams?

steps.title: Saying who gave what
steps.how_to: How to say "I gave it to you" in the past, with the right ending.
steps.intro: In the past, me lo and glielo go before ho or hai, as in te l'ho data. You'll use it to say who gave, lent or sent what.

examples.said: Le chiavi della cantina? Te le ho date io, no?
examples.en: The basement keys? I gave them to you, didn't I?

examples.said: Quel libro? Gliel'ho già ordinato.
examples.en: That book? I already ordered it for you.

examples.said: Te l'ho data ieri, la chiave.
examples.en: I gave you the key yesterday.

examples.said: Me li hai prestati tu.
examples.en: You're the one who lent them to me.

steps.notice: Lo and la shorten to l' before ho, and the ending matches the thing, data for la chiave and date for le chiavi, because it follows what was given, not the person.

ask.said: Un amico sa già la notizia. Cosa gli chiedi?
ask.en: A friend already knows the news. What do you ask him?

answer.said: Chi te l'ha detto?
answer.en: Who told you?

ask.said: Dov'è la chiave del tuo vicino?
ask.en: Where's your neighbor's key?

answer.said: Gliel'ho data ieri.
answer.en: I gave it to him yesterday.

ask.said: Hai ancora i libri della tua vicina?
ask.en: Do you still have your neighbor's books?

answer.said: No, glieli ho già restituiti.
answer.en: No, I already gave them back to her.

mission.goal: Tell your neighbor you already gave back the keys.

say.said: Te le ho già restituite ieri.
say.en: I already gave them back to you yesterday.

steps.title: Offering to do it
steps.how_to: How to use me lo or glielo with posso, può and an infinitive.
steps.intro: With posso or può, the pair goes before the verb or at the end of the infinitive, as in posso portartelo. You'll use it to offer help and to ask for it.

examples.said: Posso ordinarglielo. Arriva in due giorni.
examples.en: I can order it for you. It'll be here in two days.

examples.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
examples.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

examples.said: Me lo può spiegare?
examples.en: Could you explain it to me?

examples.said: Te lo posso portare domani.
examples.en: I can bring it to you tomorrow.

steps.notice: The pair goes before posso or può, or joins the end of the infinitive as one word, which drops its last e: portartelo; the two pronouns always stay together.

ask.said: Non capisci il modulo. Cosa chiedi all'impiegata?
ask.en: You don't understand the form. What do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Me lo può spiegare, per favore?
answer.en: Could you explain it to me, please?

ask.said: Un'amica ha bisogno del tuo caricabatterie stasera. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend needs your charger tonight. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
answer.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

ask.said: Un cliente cerca un libro, ma in negozio non c'è. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A customer is looking for a book, but it's not in the store. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Posso ordinarglielo, se vuole.
answer.en: I can order it for you, if you'd like.

mission.goal: Offer to bring something over to a friend.

say.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
say.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

steps.title: Forgetting and remembering it
steps.how_to: How to say "I forgot about it" with me ne.
steps.intro: Verbs like dimenticarsi and ricordarsi take ne for "about it," as in me ne sono dimenticato. You'll use it to apologize and to check on things.

examples.said: Me ne sono dimenticato!
examples.en: I forgot all about it!

examples.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticata!
examples.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

examples.said: Te ne sei ricordata?
examples.en: Did you remember?

examples.said: Se n'è andato presto.
examples.en: He left early.

steps.notice: Ne stands for "about it," so me ne, te ne and se ne come before the verb even where English has nothing; a woman says dimenticata.

ask.said: Non hai portato la scala alla vicina. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: You didn't bring the ladder back to your neighbor. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticato!
answer.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

ask.said: Un'amica doveva portare le chiavi. Cosa le chiedi?
ask.en: A friend was supposed to bring the keys. What do you ask her?

answer.said: Te ne sei ricordata?
answer.en: Did you remember?

ask.said: Il tuo amico non è più alla festa. Cosa è successo?
ask.en: Your friend isn't at the party anymore. What happened?

answer.said: Se n'è andato presto.
answer.en: He left early.

mission.goal: Apologize to your neighbor for forgetting something.

say.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticato!
say.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

steps.title: Describing things with che
steps.how_to: How to describe a person or thing with che.
steps.intro: Che joins two ideas, as in "the bank my landlady recommended." You'll use it to say exactly which account, card or person you mean.

examples.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
examples.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

examples.said: L'impiegata che mi ha aiutato è molto gentile.
examples.en: The clerk who helped me is really nice.

examples.said: Il conto che ho aperto è gratuito.
examples.en: The account I opened is free.

examples.said: Sì, è quella che mi avete dato la settimana scorsa.
examples.en: Yes, it's the one you gave me last week.

steps.notice: Che links a person or thing to what you say about it, whether it does the action or receives it; Italian always says che, even where English drops "that."

ask.said: Chi ti ha consigliato questa banca?
ask.en: Who recommended this bank to you?

answer.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
answer.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

ask.said: Com'è il tuo conto nuovo?
ask.en: How's your new account?

answer.said: Il conto che ho aperto è gratuito.
answer.en: The account I opened is free.

ask.said: Quale carta ti ha mangiato il bancomat?
ask.en: Which card did the ATM eat?

answer.said: Quella che mi ha dato la banca la settimana scorsa.
answer.en: The one the bank gave me last week.

mission.goal: Tell the clerk who recommended this bank.

say.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
say.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

steps.title: The person you spoke to
steps.how_to: How to say "the person I spoke to" with con cui, di cui and per cui.
steps.intro: After a word like con, di or per, Italian uses cui, as in la persona con cui ho parlato. You'll use it to explain who and what you mean at the bank.

examples.said: La persona con cui ho parlato ieri oggi non c'è.
examples.en: The person I talked to yesterday isn't here today.

examples.said: È questo il documento di cui ho bisogno?
examples.en: Is this the document I need?

examples.said: È un servizio con cui la banca paga le bollette ogni mese.
examples.en: It's a service the bank uses to pay your bills every month.

examples.said: Il titolare è la persona alla quale è intestata la carta.
examples.en: The account holder is the person whose name is on the card.

steps.notice: The little word comes first and cui follows, because an Italian sentence never ends on con or di; contracts write alla quale where people say a cui.

ask.said: Chi cerchi in banca?
ask.en: Who are you looking for at the bank?

answer.said: Cerco la persona con cui ho parlato ieri.
answer.en: I'm looking for the person I talked to yesterday.

ask.said: Perché sei in banca oggi?
ask.en: Why are you at the bank today?

answer.said: Il motivo per cui sono qui è aprire un conto.
answer.en: The reason I'm here is to open an account.

ask.said: Per aprire il conto, cosa chiedi all'impiegato?
ask.en: To open the account, what do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Qual è il documento di cui ho bisogno?
answer.en: Which document do I need?

mission.goal: Ask for the clerk you talked to yesterday.

say.said: Cerco la persona con cui ho parlato ieri.
say.en: I'm looking for the person I talked to yesterday.

steps.title: Where and when it happened
steps.how_to: How to say "the branch where" and "the day when" with dove and in cui.
steps.intro: Dove and in cui describe a place, and in cui also describes a time. You'll use them to say where your account is and when something happened.

examples.said: È la filiale dove ho il conto.
examples.en: It's the branch where I have my account.

examples.said: Questa è la filiale in cui ho aperto il conto.
examples.en: This is the branch where I opened my account.

examples.said: Il giorno in cui ho firmato il contratto, mi hanno dato il bancomat.
examples.en: The day I signed the contract, they gave me my debit card.

steps.notice: For a place you can say dove or in cui, but for a time only in cui, because dove is just for places.

ask.said: Dove vai per prelevare?
ask.en: Where do you go to take out cash?

answer.said: Vado alla filiale dove ho il conto.
answer.en: I go to the branch where I have my account.

ask.said: Quando hai ricevuto il bancomat?
ask.en: When did you get your debit card?

answer.said: Il giorno in cui ho aperto il conto.
answer.en: The day I opened my account.

ask.said: In quale filiale ritiri la carta?
ask.en: Which branch do you pick up your card at?

answer.said: In quella dove ho aperto il conto.
answer.en: At the one where I opened my account.

mission.goal: Check that you're at the branch that has your account.

say.said: È questa la filiale dove ho il conto?
say.en: Is this the branch where my account is?

steps.title: What you don't understand
steps.how_to: How to say "what" meaning "the thing that" with quello che.
steps.intro: Quello che means "what" in the sense of "the thing that." You'll use it to say what you don't understand and what you were looking for.

examples.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
examples.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

examples.said: Mi scusi, non capisco quello che dice.
examples.en: Excuse me, I don't understand what you're saying.

examples.said: È proprio quello che cercavo.
examples.en: It's just what I was looking for.

examples.said: Ciò che conta è la firma.
examples.en: What matters is the signature.

steps.notice: When "what" means "the thing that," Italian says quello che, or ciò che when it's more formal, because che alone can't stand for the thing.

ask.said: Il contratto è difficile. Cosa dici all'impiegato?
ask.en: The contract is hard to follow. What do you tell the clerk?

answer.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
answer.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

ask.said: Trovi il regalo perfetto per un'amica. Cosa dici?
ask.en: You find the perfect gift for a friend. What do you say?

answer.said: È proprio quello che cercavo!
answer.en: It's just what I was looking for!

ask.said: In un conto corrente, cosa conta di più per te?
ask.en: In a checking account, what matters most to you?

answer.said: Quello che conta è il canone mensile.
answer.en: What matters is the monthly fee.

mission.goal: Tell the clerk which part of the contract you don't understand.

say.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
say.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

steps.title: Before you sign
steps.how_to: How to say "before doing something" with prima di.
steps.intro: Prima di plus a verb means "before doing something." You'll use it at the bank to read the terms before you sign.

examples.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere le condizioni.
examples.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the terms.

examples.said: Prima di aprire il conto, mi serve il Suo codice fiscale.
examples.en: Before we open the account, I need your tax code.

examples.said: Prima di firmare, leggo sempre il contratto.
examples.en: I always read the contract before I sign.

steps.notice: "Before doing" is prima di plus the -re form of the verb, because Italian has no -ing form here.
steps.context: Many Italian checking accounts charge a monthly fee, so people ask about the spese mensili before opening one.

ask.said: L'impiegato ti dà il contratto. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: The clerk hands you the contract. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere le condizioni.
answer.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the terms.

ask.said: Cosa ti serve per aprire un conto?
ask.en: What do you need to open an account?

answer.said: Prima di aprire il conto, mi serve il codice fiscale.
answer.en: Before I open the account, I need my tax code.

ask.said: Cosa chiedi in banca prima di tutto?
ask.en: What do you ask at the bank first of all?

answer.said: Prima di aprire il conto, vorrei sapere le spese mensili.
answer.en: Before I open the account, I'd like to know the monthly fees.

mission.goal: Ask to read the terms before you sign.

say.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere le condizioni.
say.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the terms.

steps.title: Comparing two apartments
steps.how_to: How to say "than" with di or che when you compare.
steps.intro: To compare two things, Italian says "than" with di or with che. You'll use it to weigh up two apartments.

examples.said: Questo è più luminoso dell'altro.
examples.en: This one's brighter than the other one.

examples.said: Sì, ma è più piccolo di questo.
examples.en: Yes, but it's smaller than this one.

examples.said: La strada è più rumorosa di giorno che di notte.
examples.en: The street is noisier during the day than at night.

examples.said: È più bello che comodo.
examples.en: It's more beautiful than comfortable.

steps.notice: Before a thing or a word like questo, "than" is di; before an adjective or a phrase like di notte it's che, because you're comparing two qualities or two times of the same thing.

ask.said: Hai visto due appartamenti. Com'è il primo rispetto al secondo?
ask.en: You saw two apartments. How does the first compare to the second?

answer.said: Il primo è più grande del secondo.
answer.en: The first one is bigger than the second.

ask.said: Il monolocale ti piace?
ask.en: Do you like the studio?

answer.said: Sì, ma è più bello che comodo.
answer.en: Yes, but it's more beautiful than comfortable.

ask.said: Com'è la tua strada, di giorno e di notte?
ask.en: What's your street like, during the day and at night?

answer.said: È più rumorosa di giorno che di notte.
answer.en: It's noisier during the day than at night.

mission.goal: Compare two apartments with a friend.

say.said: Questo è più luminoso dell'altro.
say.en: This one's brighter than the other one.

steps.title: The best and the worst
steps.how_to: How to say "the most," "the best" and "very" about a place.
steps.intro: Il più says "the most," il migliore says "the best," and -issimo says "very." You'll use them to pick an apartment and talk about the neighborhood.

examples.said: È il più grande che abbiamo visto.
examples.en: It's the biggest one we've seen.

examples.said: Allora secondo me è il migliore.
examples.en: Then I think it's the best one.

examples.said: È il bilocale più luminoso del palazzo.
examples.en: It's the brightest one-bedroom in the building.

examples.said: La zona è tranquillissima.
examples.en: The neighborhood is really quiet.

steps.notice: "The most" is il più plus the adjective, with di for the group, as in del palazzo; il migliore already means "the best," and -issimo means "very."

ask.said: Com'è la tua zona?
ask.en: What's your neighborhood like?

answer.said: È tranquillissima.
answer.en: It's really quiet.

ask.said: Hai visto tre bilocali. Quale prendi?
ask.en: You saw three one-bedrooms. Which one are you taking?

answer.said: Prendo questo: è il più luminoso dei tre.
answer.en: I'm taking this one. It's the brightest of the three.

ask.said: E l'appartamento vicino al mercato, com'era?
ask.en: And the apartment near the market, what was it like?

answer.said: Era pessimo.
answer.en: It was terrible.

mission.goal: Tell a friend which apartment is the best.

say.said: Secondo me questo è il migliore.
say.en: I think this one's the best.

steps.title: How long it's been
steps.how_to: How to say how long something has been going on with sono... che.
steps.intro: Sono due settimane che plus the present says how long something has been going on. You'll use it to chase a repair with your landlady.

examples.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
examples.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

examples.said: È un mese che il citofono non funziona.
examples.en: The buzzer hasn't worked in a month.

examples.said: Abito qui da sei mesi.
examples.en: I've lived here for six months.

steps.notice: For something that started in the past and is still going on, Italian uses the present, because it isn't over: sono due settimane che aspetto, or aspetto da due settimane; with one week or month, it's è.

ask.said: Da quanto tempo abiti qui?
ask.en: How long have you lived here?

answer.said: Abito qui da … mesi.
answer.en: I've lived here for … months.

ask.said: La caldaia è ancora rotta. Cosa dici alla padrona di casa?
ask.en: The boiler's still broken. What do you tell your landlady?

answer.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
answer.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

ask.said: Il citofono è ancora rotto. Cosa dici all'amministratore?
ask.en: The buzzer's still broken. What do you tell the building manager?

answer.said: È un mese che il citofono non funziona.
answer.en: The buzzer hasn't worked in a month.

mission.goal: Tell your landlady how long you've been waiting for the plumber.

say.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
say.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

steps.title: Describing the one you want
steps.how_to: How to describe an apartment or a person with che and in cui.
steps.intro: Che and in cui let you say which apartment, area or person you mean. You'll use them when you choose a place and deal with repairs.

examples.said: Allora, prendi il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri?
examples.en: So, are you taking the one-bedroom we saw yesterday?

examples.said: La zona in cui vorrei vivere è vicino al mercato.
examples.en: The area I'd like to live in is near the market.

examples.said: L'idraulico che chiamo di solito è in ferie.
examples.en: The plumber I usually call is on vacation.

steps.notice: To say which one you mean, add che plus what you say about it, or a little word like in plus cui, as in la zona in cui vorrei vivere.

ask.said: Quale appartamento ti piace di più?
ask.en: Which apartment do you like best?

answer.said: Mi piace il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri.
answer.en: I like the one-bedroom we saw yesterday.

ask.said: In quale zona vorresti vivere?
ask.en: What area would you like to live in?

answer.said: La zona in cui vorrei vivere è vicino a …
answer.en: The area I'd like to live in is near …

ask.said: Chi chiami se la caldaia è rotta?
ask.en: Who do you call if the boiler breaks?

answer.said: Chiamo l'idraulico che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
answer.en: I call the plumber my landlady recommended.

mission.goal: Tell a friend which apartment you prefer.

say.said: Preferisco il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri.
say.en: I prefer the one-bedroom we saw yesterday.

steps.title: Comparing travel options
steps.how_to: How to compare two options and pick the best one.
steps.intro: You'll be able to weigh the train against the bus, or one hotel against another, when you plan a trip. These are comparisons: more than, less than, as much as, and the most.

examples.said: Il treno è più veloce del pullman.
examples.en: The train is faster than the bus.

examples.said: Il treno è più comodo, ma il pullman costa meno.
examples.en: The train is more comfortable, but the bus is cheaper.

examples.said: Il B&B costa tanto quanto l'albergo.
examples.en: The B&B costs as much as the hotel.

examples.said: È l'albergo più tranquillo della zona.
examples.en: It's the quietest hotel in the area.

steps.notice: Più or meno with di compares two things (più veloce del pullman), tanto quanto says they're the same, and il più with di picks the top one out of a group: l'albergo più tranquillo della zona.

ask.said: Per un weekend a Napoli, prendi il treno o il pullman? Perché?
ask.en: For a weekend in Naples, are you taking the train or the bus? Why?

answer.said: Prendo il treno, perché è più veloce del pullman.
answer.en: I'm taking the train, because it's faster than the bus.

ask.said: Com'è il B&B rispetto all'albergo?
ask.en: How does the B&B compare with the hotel?

answer.said: Il B&B costa tanto quanto l'albergo, ma è più tranquillo.
answer.en: The B&B costs as much as the hotel, but it's quieter.

ask.said: Qui in zona, che albergo consigli a un amico?
ask.en: Around here, which hotel would you recommend to a friend?

answer.said: L'albergo … è il più tranquillo della zona.
answer.en: The … is the quietest hotel in the area.

mission.goal: Compare the train and the bus with a friend.

say.said: Il treno è più comodo, ma il pullman costa meno.
say.en: The train is more comfortable, but the bus is cheaper.

steps.title: Making it and getting by
steps.how_to: How to say you can make it, you're getting by, you're leaving, or not to let something get to you.
steps.intro: Some everyday verbs come with two little words attached, like ce la fai or me la cavo, and friends use them all the time when they plan a trip. You'll be able to ask if someone can make it, say you're managing, say you're leaving, and tell someone not to get upset.

examples.said: Ce la fai per le otto?
examples.en: Can you make it by eight?

examples.said: Me la cavo, grazie.
examples.en: I'm managing, thanks.

examples.said: Domani mattina ce ne andiamo presto.
examples.en: We're leaving early tomorrow morning.

examples.said: Non te la prendere, capita.
examples.en: Don't let it get to you, it happens.

steps.notice: The little words are part of each verb and don't mean 'it' or 'there' anymore, and the first one changes with the person: ce la faccio, ce la fai; me la cavo, te la cavi.

ask.said: Domani il treno parte alle sette. Riesci a essere in stazione in tempo?
ask.en: The train leaves at seven tomorrow. Can you get to the station in time?

answer.said: Sì, ce la faccio.
answer.en: Yes, I can make it.

ask.said: Come va con l'italiano qui?
ask.en: How's your Italian going here?

answer.said: Me la cavo, grazie.
answer.en: I'm getting by, thanks.

ask.said: Un amico ha perso il treno ed è arrabbiato. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend missed his train and he's upset. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Non te la prendere, capita.
answer.en: Don't let it get to you, it happens.

mission.goal: Tell someone how you're getting on with Italian.

say.said: Me la cavo, grazie.
say.en: I'm getting by, thanks.

steps.title: Saying nobody helped
steps.how_to: How to say nobody did something, with nessuno first or after the verb.
steps.intro: When something goes wrong on a trip, you'll want to say nobody came or nobody helped. Nessuno can start the sentence or come after the verb.

examples.said: Nessuno ci ha aiutato.
examples.en: Nobody helped us.

examples.said: Non ci ha aiutato nessuno.
examples.en: Nobody helped us.

examples.said: Non c'era nessuno alla reception.
examples.en: There was nobody at the front desk.

examples.said: Davvero? Non è venuto nessuno?
examples.en: Really? Nobody came?

steps.notice: Both ways mean the same thing: at the start, nessuno stands on its own; after the verb, it goes with non before the verb, so the sentence is negative from the beginning.

ask.said: Quando hai fatto il check-in, chi c'era alla reception?
ask.en: When you checked in, who was at the front desk?

answer.said: Non c'era nessuno alla reception.
answer.en: There was nobody at the front desk.

ask.said: Hai chiamato la reception due volte. Chi ti ha aiutato?
ask.en: You called the front desk twice. Who helped you?

answer.said: Nessuno mi ha aiutato.
answer.en: Nobody helped me.

ask.said: E dopo la seconda telefonata, è venuto qualcuno?
ask.en: And after the second call, did anyone come?

answer.said: No, non è venuto nessuno.
answer.en: No, nobody came.

mission.goal: Tell a friend about a stay where nobody helped you.

say.said: Nessuno ci ha aiutato.
say.en: Nobody helped us.

steps.title: Telling what went wrong
steps.how_to: How to say how things were on a stay and what happened next.
steps.intro: You'll be able to tell what went wrong on a trip: how the room was, then what you did about it. That's the imperfetto for how things were and the passato prossimo for what happened.

examples.said: La camera era piccola e faceva freddo.
examples.en: The room was small and it was cold.

examples.said: Quando siamo arrivati, la camera era sporca.
examples.en: When we got there, the room was dirty.

examples.said: L'aria condizionata non funzionava e abbiamo chiamato due volte.
examples.en: The air conditioning wasn't working, and we called twice.

examples.said: E poi? Vi hanno cambiato la camera?
examples.en: And then? Did they give you a different room?

steps.notice: Era, faceva and non funzionava describe how things were, while siamo arrivati, abbiamo chiamato and hanno cambiato tell what happened, one event after another.

ask.said: Pensa a un viaggio andato male. Com'era la camera?
ask.en: Think of a trip that went badly. What was the room like?

answer.said: La camera era piccola e sporca.
answer.en: The room was small and dirty.

ask.said: Che problemi c'erano in camera?
ask.en: What was wrong with the room?

answer.said: L'aria condizionata non funzionava e faceva caldo.
answer.en: The air conditioning wasn't working, and it was hot.

ask.said: E tu cosa hai fatto?
ask.en: And what did you do?

answer.said: Ho chiamato la reception e mi hanno cambiato la camera.
answer.en: I called the front desk, and they gave me a different room.

mission.goal: Tell a friend what went wrong on a trip.

say.said: La camera era sporca e abbiamo chiamato la reception.
say.en: The room was dirty, and we called the front desk.

b1-06.title: Telling it well: longer stories and clarifying

steps.title: What had already happened
steps.how_to: How to say one thing had already happened before another.
steps.intro: When you tell a story, you'll be able to say what had already happened by then, like the train had already left. It's the trapassato: the imperfetto of avere or essere plus the past participle.

examples.said: Quando siamo arrivati, il treno era già partito.
examples.en: When we got there, the train had already left.

examples.said: Sul treno ho capito che avevo dimenticato il caricabatterie a casa.
examples.en: On the train I realized I'd left my charger at home.

examples.said: Non avevo mai visto tanta gente.
examples.en: I'd never seen so many people.

examples.said: Quando è saltata la luce, avevo già cenato.
examples.en: When the power went out, I'd already had dinner.

steps.notice: Era partito and avevo dimenticato put one past event before another, because it happened first; essere and avere work just as in the passato prossimo.

ask.said: Ieri hai perso il treno. Perché?
ask.en: You missed your train yesterday. Why?

answer.said: Quando ho trovato il binario, il treno era già partito.
answer.en: By the time I found the platform, the train had already left.

ask.said: Sul treno hai aperto lo zaino. Cosa mancava?
ask.en: On the train you opened your backpack. What was missing?

answer.said: Avevo dimenticato il caricabatterie a casa.
answer.en: I'd left my charger at home.

ask.said: Cosa hai visto qui in Italia per la prima volta?
ask.en: What did you see here in Italy for the first time?

answer.said: Non avevo mai visto tanta gente in piazza.
answer.en: I'd never seen so many people in a piazza.

mission.goal: Tell a friend about a time you got there too late.

say.said: Quando siamo arrivati, il treno era già partito.
say.en: When we got there, the train had already left.

steps.title: Linking causes and results
steps.how_to: How to give the reason for something and what came of it.
steps.intro: You'll be able to link why something happened and what happened next when you tell a story. Siccome and visto che open with the reason, perché gives it after, and quindi, perciò and così bring in the result.

examples.said: Siccome pioveva, abbiamo preso un taxi.
examples.en: Since it was raining, we took a taxi.

examples.said: Abbiamo preso un taxi perché pioveva.
examples.en: We took a taxi because it was raining.

examples.said: Visto che c'era sciopero, siamo andati a piedi.
examples.en: Since there was a strike, we walked.

examples.said: Ormai era tardi, quindi ho cenato con pane e formaggio.
examples.en: By then it was late, so I had bread and cheese for dinner.

steps.notice: Siccome and visto che put the reason first, perché puts it after what happened, and quindi brings in the result, so you can tell the same story in either order.
steps.context: Strikes are announced days in advance, and a story that starts with c'era sciopero is one every Italian recognizes.

ask.said: Ieri pioveva tanto. Come hai fatto a tornare a casa?
ask.en: It poured yesterday. How did you get home?

answer.said: Siccome pioveva, ho preso un taxi.
answer.en: Since it was raining, I took a taxi.

ask.said: Perché non hai preso l'autobus?
ask.en: Why didn't you take the bus?

answer.said: Non ho preso l'autobus perché c'era sciopero.
answer.en: I didn't take the bus because there was a strike.

ask.said: Ieri c'era sciopero dei treni. Cosa hai fatto?
ask.en: There was a train strike yesterday. What did you do?

answer.said: C'era sciopero, quindi ho preso il pullman.
answer.en: There was a strike, so I took the bus.

mission.goal: Tell a friend why something went wrong and what you did.

say.said: Siccome c'era sciopero, ho preso un taxi.
say.en: Since there was a strike, I took a taxi.

steps.title: In the middle of it
steps.how_to: How to say what you were doing, or about to do, when something happened.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say what you were in the middle of when something happened, or what you were just about to do. Stavo plus the -ando or -endo form means in the middle of; stavo per plus a verb means about to.

examples.said: Stavo cucinando quando è saltata la luce.
examples.en: I was cooking when the power went out.

examples.said: Anch'io ero a casa. Stavo per andare a letto.
examples.en: I was home too. I was about to go to bed.

examples.said: Stavo per chiamarti!
examples.en: I was just about to call you!

examples.said: Il treno stava per partire.
examples.en: The train was about to leave.

steps.notice: Stavo cucinando is something already under way, and stavo per andare is something that hadn't started yet, because per points ahead to what comes next.

ask.said: Ieri sera è saltata la luce. Tu cosa facevi?
ask.en: The power went out last night. What were you doing?

answer.said: Stavo cucinando quando è saltata la luce.
answer.en: I was cooking when the power went out.

ask.said: Ti ho chiamato alle undici. Dormivi già?
ask.en: I called you at eleven. Were you already asleep?

answer.said: No, stavo per andare a letto.
answer.en: No, I was about to go to bed.

ask.said: Un amico ti telefona. Anche tu volevi chiamarlo. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend calls you. You were going to call him too. What do you say?

answer.said: Stavo per chiamarti!
answer.en: I was just about to call you!

mission.goal: Tell a neighbor what you were doing when the power went out.

say.said: Stavo cucinando quando è saltata la luce.
say.en: I was cooking when the power went out.

steps.title: Saying what you mean
steps.how_to: How to put something another way and ask what someone means.
steps.intro: When someone misunderstands you, or you don't follow them, you'll be able to clear it up in Italian instead of switching to English.

examples.said: In che senso? Mi spieghi?
examples.en: What do you mean? Can you explain?

examples.said: Cioè, voglio dire che è stancante.
examples.en: I mean, what I'm saying is it's tiring.

examples.said: Mi spiego meglio: sono quattro ore di fila, senza pausa.
examples.en: Let me put it another way: it's four hours straight, with no break.

examples.said: Nel senso che non ho tempo.
examples.en: Meaning I don't have time.

steps.notice: Cioè, voglio dire, nel senso che and mi spiego meglio let you say the same thing another way, and in che senso? asks the other person to do it.

ask.said: Hai detto che il corso è pesante. È difficile?
ask.en: You said the course is heavy going. Is it hard?

answer.said: No, cioè, voglio dire che è stancante.
answer.en: No, I mean, what I'm saying is it's tiring.

ask.said: Non capisci cosa vuole dire un amico. Cosa gli chiedi?
ask.en: You don't get what a friend means. What do you ask him?

answer.said: In che senso? Mi spieghi?
answer.en: What do you mean? Can you explain?

ask.said: Il tuo amico non ha ancora capito. Cosa dici?
ask.en: Your friend still doesn't get it. What do you say?

answer.said: Mi spiego meglio: sono quattro ore di fila.
answer.en: Let me put it another way: it's four hours straight.

mission.goal: When someone doesn't follow you, say it another way in Italian.

say.said: Mi spiego meglio.
say.en: Let me put it another way.

b1-07.title: Opinions, hopes and doubts: the subjunctive

steps.title: New endings for opinions
steps.how_to: How to form the verbs that come after penso che and spero che.
steps.intro: You'll learn the forms of the subjunctive, the verbs Italians use after an opinion or a hope. Verbs in -are take -i, the others take -a, and a few common verbs have their own forms, like sia, abbia, faccia and venga.

examples.said: Penso che Marco parli bene.
examples.en: I think Marco speaks well.

examples.said: Spero che venga anche Marco.
examples.en: I hope Marco comes too.

examples.said: Credo che abbiano ragione.
examples.en: I think they're right.

examples.said: Penso che tu abbia ragione.
examples.en: I think you're right.

steps.notice: After penso che and spero che the verb changes its ending: parli, venga, abbia, abbiano. Io, tu and lei share one form, so add tu when you mean the person you're talking to.

ask.said: Viene anche Marco stasera?
ask.en: Is Marco coming tonight too?

answer.said: Spero che venga anche lui.
answer.en: I hope he's coming too.

ask.said: Io dico che il museo è chiuso. Ho ragione?
ask.en: I say the museum is closed. Am I right?

answer.said: Penso che tu abbia ragione.
answer.en: I think you're right.

ask.said: Il tuo vicino parla inglese?
ask.en: Does your neighbor speak English?

answer.said: Credo che parli un po' d'inglese.
answer.en: I think he speaks a little English.

mission.goal: Tell someone you think they're right.

say.said: Penso che tu abbia ragione.
say.en: I think you're right.

steps.title: Guessing and hoping
steps.how_to: How to say what you think, hope or doubt when you're not sure.
steps.intro: You'll be able to guess whether a museum is open, or say what you hope or doubt. After penso che, spero che, non credo che, mi sembra che, può darsi che and ho l'impressione che, the verb is in the subjunctive.

examples.said: Domani è lunedì. Penso che sia chiuso il lunedì.
examples.en: Tomorrow's Monday. I think it's closed on Mondays.

examples.said: Non credo che sia così semplice.
examples.en: I don't think it's that simple.

examples.said: Può darsi che tu abbia ragione.
examples.en: You may be right.

examples.said: Ho l'impressione che qui si ceni molto tardi.
examples.en: I get the feeling people eat dinner really late here.

steps.notice: Each line starts with an opinion, a hope or a doubt, so the verb after che is sia, abbia or ceni, because it's what you think, not a fact.
steps.context: Many museums and shops close one day a week, often Monday, so penso che sia chiuso il lunedì is a guess you'll make a lot.

ask.said: Oggi è lunedì. Il museo è aperto?
ask.en: It's Monday today. Is the museum open?

answer.said: Penso che sia chiuso il lunedì.
answer.en: I think it's closed on Mondays.

ask.said: Che tempo farà domenica?
ask.en: What's the weather going to be like on Sunday?

answer.said: Spero che faccia bel tempo.
answer.en: I hope it'll be nice out.

ask.said: Com'è la vita qui rispetto a casa tua?
ask.en: How's life here compared to back home?

answer.said: Ho l'impressione che qui si ceni molto tardi.
answer.en: I get the feeling people eat dinner really late here.

mission.goal: Guess with someone whether a place is open today.

say.said: Penso che sia chiuso il lunedì.
say.en: I think it's closed on Mondays.

steps.title: Hoping to do something
steps.how_to: How to say what you hope or think you'll do yourself.
steps.intro: When you talk about your own plans, like going home for Christmas, you'll be able to say spero di tornare. When the one hoping is the one doing it, use di plus the infinitive.

examples.said: Spero di tornare a casa per Natale.
examples.en: I hope to go home for Christmas.

examples.said: Penso di restare un altro anno.
examples.en: I think I'll stay another year.

examples.said: Credo di aver capito.
examples.en: I think I've got it.

examples.said: Spero di abituarmi presto!
examples.en: I hope I get used to it soon!

steps.notice: When you're both the one hoping and the one doing, use di plus the infinitive (spero di tornare), because the subject is the same person.

ask.said: Torni a casa per Natale?
ask.en: Are you going home for Christmas?

answer.said: Spero di tornare a casa per Natale.
answer.en: I hope to go home for Christmas.

ask.said: Quanto tempo resti in Italia?
ask.en: How long are you staying in Italy?

answer.said: Penso di restare un altro anno.
answer.en: I think I'll stay another year.

ask.said: Come va con gli orari dei pasti qui?
ask.en: How are you doing with mealtimes here?

answer.said: Spero di abituarmi presto!
answer.en: I hope I get used to them soon!

mission.goal: Tell a friend what you hope to do over the holidays.

say.said: Spero di tornare a casa per Natale.
say.en: I hope to go home for Christmas.

steps.title: Facts and plain opinions
steps.how_to: How to state a fact or give your view straight out.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say what you know for sure, or give your view plainly. So che, sono sicuro che, è vero che and secondo me take the ordinary verb forms, the indicative.

examples.said: So che è chiuso il lunedì.
examples.en: I know it's closed on Mondays.

examples.said: Secondo me è chiuso.
examples.en: If you ask me, it's closed.

examples.said: È vero che qui si cena tardi.
examples.en: It's true people eat late here.

examples.said: Secondo me è un po' caro.
examples.en: If you ask me, it's a little expensive.

steps.notice: So che, è vero che and secondo me present something as a fact or a plain view, so the verb stays as usual: è chiuso, si cena.

ask.said: Secondo te, quel ristorante è caro?
ask.en: Do you think that restaurant is expensive?

answer.said: Secondo me è un po' caro.
answer.en: If you ask me, it's a little expensive.

ask.said: Hai controllato gli orari del museo. È aperto il martedì?
ask.en: You checked the museum's hours. Is it open on Tuesdays?

answer.said: No, so che è chiuso il martedì.
answer.en: No, I know it's closed on Tuesdays.

ask.said: A che ora si cena al sud?
ask.en: What time do people eat dinner in the south?

answer.said: So che al sud si cena verso le nove o le dieci.
answer.en: I know in the south people eat around nine or ten.

mission.goal: Give a friend your opinion of a restaurant.

say.said: Secondo me è un po' caro.
say.en: If you ask me, it's a little expensive.

steps.title: Saying I think so
steps.how_to: How to answer I think so or I don't think so.
steps.intro: When someone asks a yes-or-no question and you're not sure, you'll be able to answer in a few words: penso di sì, credo di no. You'll also hear penso che è in relaxed speech, but careful speakers use the subjunctive.

examples.said: I biglietti costano tanto?
examples.en: Are the tickets expensive?

examples.said: Penso di sì.
examples.en: I think so.

examples.said: Viene anche lui?
examples.en: Is he coming too?

examples.said: Credo di no.
examples.en: I don't think so.

steps.notice: Penso di sì, credo di no and spero di sì answer a yes-or-no question on their own, always with di before sì or no.

ask.said: Il museo è aperto domani?
ask.en: Is the museum open tomorrow?

answer.said: Penso di sì.
answer.en: I think so.

ask.said: Domani piove?
ask.en: Is it going to rain tomorrow?

answer.said: Spero di no!
answer.en: I hope not!

ask.said: C'è un volo diretto per casa tua?
ask.en: Is there a direct flight to where you're from?

answer.said: Credo di no.
answer.en: I don't think so.

mission.goal: Answer someone's question with I think so or I don't think so.

say.said: Penso di sì.
say.en: I think so.

b1-08.title: Advice, needs and a healthy life

steps.title: Giving someone advice
steps.how_to: How to give advice to one person, or general advice to anyone.
steps.intro: You'll be able to give advice, and follow a pharmacist's: you'd better not, it's important that you. For one person it's che plus the subjunctive; for anyone at all, just the infinitive.

examples.said: È meglio che Lei non beva caffè dopo pranzo.
examples.en: You'd better not have coffee after lunch.

examples.said: Bisogna che faccia un po' di movimento ogni giorno.
examples.en: You need to get a little exercise every day.

examples.said: È importante che tu faccia almeno mezz'ora di movimento al giorno.
examples.en: It's important that you get at least half an hour of exercise a day.

examples.said: È meglio non bere caffè la sera.
examples.en: It's better not to drink coffee in the evening.

steps.notice: For one person, è meglio che, è importante che and bisogna che take the subjunctive (beva, faccia); for advice to anyone, use the infinitive, because there's no one in particular.
steps.context: Pharmacists give real advice and suggest remedies, so the pharmacy is the first stop for small health problems.

ask.said: Un amico dorme male. Cosa gli consigli?
ask.en: A friend is sleeping badly. What would you tell him?

answer.said: È meglio che tu non beva caffè la sera.
answer.en: You'd better not drink coffee in the evening.

ask.said: Un'amica non fa mai sport. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend never exercises. What do you tell her?

answer.said: È importante che tu faccia almeno mezz'ora di movimento al giorno.
answer.en: It's important that you get at least half an hour of exercise a day.

ask.said: Secondo te, cos'è importante per dormire bene?
ask.en: What do you think matters for sleeping well?

answer.said: È importante non bere caffè la sera.
answer.en: It's important not to drink coffee in the evening.

mission.goal: Give a friend advice about sleeping better.

say.said: È meglio che tu non beva caffè la sera.
say.en: You'd better not drink coffee in the evening.

steps.title: Setting a condition
steps.how_to: How to agree to something as long as, or unless, something happens.
steps.intro: You'll be able to agree to something on a condition, like lending your bike as long as it comes back tonight. Purché means as long as, a meno che non means unless, and both take the subjunctive.

examples.said: Ti presto la bici, purché tu me la riporti stasera.
examples.en: I'll lend you the bike, as long as you bring it back tonight.

examples.said: A meno che non piova, domani andiamo al mare.
examples.en: Unless it rains, we'll go to the beach tomorrow.

examples.said: Promesso. A meno che non me la rubino al mercato!
examples.en: I promise. Unless someone steals it at the market!

steps.notice: Purché sets the condition and a meno che non names what would stop it; both take the subjunctive (riporti, piova), and the non after a meno che doesn't make it negative.

ask.said: Un'amica ti chiede la bici. Cosa le rispondi?
ask.en: A friend asks to borrow your bike. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Te la presto, purché tu me la riporti stasera.
answer.en: Sure, as long as you bring it back tonight.

ask.said: Domani andiamo al mare?
ask.en: Should we go to the beach tomorrow?

answer.said: Sì, a meno che non piova.
answer.en: Yes, unless it rains.

ask.said: Un amico vuole la tua macchina per il weekend. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend wants your car for the weekend. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Te la presto, purché tu me la riporti domenica.
answer.en: Sure, as long as you bring it back on Sunday.

mission.goal: Lend a friend something on a condition.

say.said: Te la presto, purché tu me la riporti stasera.
say.en: Sure, as long as you bring it back tonight.

steps.title: Before I go, before you go
steps.how_to: How to say before with the same person or with someone else.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say what you'll do before you leave, or before someone else does something. Prima di plus the infinitive is for the same person; prima che plus the subjunctive is for someone or something else.

examples.said: Prima di partire, ti chiamo.
examples.en: I'll call you before I leave.

examples.said: Prima che tu parta, ti do il mio numero.
examples.en: Before you leave, I'll give you my number.

examples.said: Te la riporto prima che faccia buio.
examples.en: I'll bring it back before it gets dark.

steps.notice: Use prima di plus the infinitive when you're the one doing both things, and prima che plus the subjunctive when the second part is about someone else, or even the weather.

ask.said: Parti domani. Cosa fai stasera?
ask.en: You're leaving tomorrow. What are you doing tonight?

answer.said: Prima di partire, faccio la valigia.
answer.en: I'm packing before I leave.

ask.said: Un'amica parte per Napoli domani. Cosa le dai?
ask.en: A friend is leaving for Naples tomorrow. What do you give her?

answer.said: Prima che tu parta, ti do il mio numero.
answer.en: Before you leave, I'll give you my number.

ask.said: La tua amica ti ha prestato la bici. Quando gliela riporti?
ask.en: Your friend lent you her bike. When will you bring it back to her?

answer.said: Gliela riporto prima che faccia buio.
answer.en: I'll bring it back to her before it gets dark.

mission.goal: Tell a friend you'll give them your number before they leave.

say.said: Prima che tu parta, ti do il mio numero.
say.en: Before you leave, I'll give you my number.

steps.title: Hoping it went well
steps.how_to: How to hope or think something has already happened.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say you hope someone slept well, or think someone has already arrived. It's the past subjunctive: abbia or sia plus the past participle.

examples.said: Spero che tu abbia dormito bene.
examples.en: I hope you slept well.

examples.said: Credo che sia già arrivata.
examples.en: I think she's already here.

examples.said: Non penso che abbiano capito.
examples.en: I don't think they understood.

examples.said: Penso che Anna sia arrivata ieri.
examples.en: I think Anna got here yesterday.

steps.notice: After spero che, credo che and penso che, something already done takes abbia or sia plus the participle, and with sia the participle agrees, just as in Anna è arrivata.

ask.said: Un'amica ieri sera era molto stanca. Cosa le dici stamattina?
ask.en: A friend was really tired last night. What do you say to her this morning?

answer.said: Spero che tu abbia dormito bene.
answer.en: I hope you slept well.

ask.said: Anna doveva arrivare alle dieci. Dov'è, secondo te?
ask.en: Anna was supposed to arrive at ten. Where do you think she is?

answer.said: Penso che sia già arrivata a casa.
answer.en: I think she's already gotten home.

ask.said: Hai spiegato la strada a due turisti. Hanno capito?
ask.en: You gave two tourists directions. Did they understand?

answer.said: Non penso che abbiano capito.
answer.en: I don't think they understood.

mission.goal: Greet a friend by saying you hope they slept well.

say.said: Spero che tu abbia dormito bene.
say.en: I hope you slept well.

steps.title: Even though it's cold
steps.how_to: How to say you do something even though there's a reason not to.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say you do something anyway, like going running even though it's cold. Anche se and benché both mean even though, but only benché takes the subjunctive.

examples.said: Anche se fa freddo, esco.
examples.en: Even though it's cold, I'm going out.

examples.said: Benché faccia freddo, vado a correre.
examples.en: Even though it's cold, I'm going running.

examples.said: Anche se piove, vado a correre.
examples.en: Even if it rains, I'm going running.

examples.said: Vado a correre tre volte a settimana, benché faccia freddo.
examples.en: I go running three times a week, even though it's cold.

steps.notice: Anche se keeps the usual verb (fa, piove), and benché takes the subjunctive (faccia), because benché is one of the words that always needs it.

ask.said: Oggi fa freddo. Esci lo stesso?
ask.en: It's cold today. Are you going out anyway?

answer.said: Sì, benché faccia freddo, esco lo stesso.
answer.en: Yes, even though it's cold, I'm going out anyway.

ask.said: Mangi sano?
ask.en: Do you eat healthy?

answer.said: Sì, anche se non rinuncio alla pizza del sabato!
answer.en: Yes, even though I'm not giving up my Saturday pizza!

ask.said: Hai poco tempo. Vai in palestra stasera?
ask.en: You're short on time. Are you going to the gym tonight?

answer.said: Sì, anche se ho poco tempo, ci vado.
answer.en: Yes, even though I'm short on time, I'm going.

mission.goal: Tell a friend you exercise even when the weather's bad.

say.said: Anche se piove, vado a correre.
say.en: Even if it rains, I'm going running.

steps.title: Telling a driver where to go
steps.how_to: How to tell someone you call Lei what to do, like a taxi driver.
steps.intro: This is how you ask someone you call Lei to do something, like a taxi driver or a stranger in the street. It uses the same forms as the present subjunctive.

examples.said: Giri alla prima a destra, per favore.
examples.en: Take the first right, please.

examples.said: Vada un po' più avanti, per favore.
examples.en: Go a little farther, please.

examples.said: Vada sempre dritto, poi giri a destra.
examples.en: Go straight ahead, then turn right.

examples.said: Prenda il primo autobus.
examples.en: Take the first bus.

steps.notice: With Lei, verbs ending in -are take an -i (giri) and the others take an -a (prenda), the opposite of the tu forms; andare becomes vada. That's because this command is really the subjunctive.
steps.context: In most Italian cities you take a taxi from a rank or book one by phone or app.

ask.said: Un turista anziano ti chiede la strada per la piazza. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: An older tourist asks you the way to the piazza. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Vada sempre dritto, poi giri a destra.
answer.en: Go straight ahead, then turn right.

ask.said: Sei in taxi e il tassista non conosce la tua via. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: You're in a taxi and the driver doesn't know your street. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Giri alla prima a destra e vada più avanti.
answer.en: Take the first right and keep going.

ask.said: Una signora vuole andare in centro in autobus. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A woman wants to take the bus downtown. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Prenda il primo autobus.
answer.en: Take the first bus.

mission.goal: Give a taxi driver directions to your street.

say.said: Giri alla prima a destra, per favore.
say.en: Take the first right, please.

steps.title: Have a seat, how can I help
steps.how_to: How to place mi and si when you ask someone you call Lei to do something.
steps.intro: Today you'll learn the polite phrases staff use with you, like mi dica and si accomodi, and how to say them yourself. With Lei, the little words mi and si come first.

examples.said: Buongiorno, mi dica.
examples.en: Good morning, how can I help you?

examples.said: Prego, si accomodi.
examples.en: Please, have a seat.

examples.said: Mi porti in via Veneto, per favore.
examples.en: Take me to Via Veneto, please.

examples.said: Mi faccia anche la ricevuta, per favore.
examples.en: Could I get a receipt too, please?

steps.notice: With Lei, mi and si always go before the verb: mi dica, si accomodi, mi porti. That's different from tu commands like dimmi, where they go on the end.
steps.context: At the end of a taxi ride, you can ask the driver for a receipt, la ricevuta.

ask.said: Una signora anziana entra e cerca una sedia. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: An older woman comes in, looking for a chair. What do you say to her?

answer.said: Prego, si accomodi.
answer.en: Please, have a seat.

ask.said: Sei in taxi e vuoi andare in via Veneto. Cosa dici al tassista?
ask.en: You're in a taxi and you want to go to Via Veneto. What do you tell the driver?

answer.said: Mi porti in via Veneto, per favore.
answer.en: Take me to Via Veneto, please.

ask.said: Lavori in un ufficio e arriva un signore. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: You work in an office and a man comes in. What do you say to him?

answer.said: Buongiorno, mi dica.
answer.en: Good morning, how can I help you?

mission.goal: Offer an older neighbor a seat.

say.said: Prego, si accomodi.
say.en: Please, have a seat.

steps.title: Telling someone not to worry
steps.how_to: How to tell someone you call Lei not to do something.
steps.intro: Now you'll tell someone you call Lei not to do something, most often not to worry. You'll hear non si preoccupi all the time.

examples.said: Non si preoccupi, Le tengo io il posto.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'll save your seat.

examples.said: Non si preoccupi, glielo prendo io.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'll take it in for you.

examples.said: Non lo tocchi, per favore.
examples.en: Please don't touch it.

examples.said: Non se ne vada, arrivo subito!
examples.en: Don't leave, I'll be right with you!

steps.notice: Put non in front of the same polite form and keep si or lo before the verb: non si preoccupi, non lo tocchi. Nothing else changes.

ask.said: Il tuo vicino aspetta un pacco, ma domani non è a casa. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: Your neighbor is expecting a package, but he won't be home tomorrow. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Non si preoccupi, glielo prendo io.
answer.en: Don't worry, I'll take it in for you.

ask.said: In sala d'attesa, una signora deve uscire un momento. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: In the waiting room, a woman needs to step out for a moment. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Non si preoccupi, Le tengo io il posto.
answer.en: Don't worry, I'll save your seat.

ask.said: Lavori in un negozio e un cliente vuole andare via. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: You work in a shop and a customer wants to leave. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Non se ne vada, arrivo subito!
answer.en: Don't leave, I'll be right with you!

mission.goal: Reassure an older neighbor who needs a hand.

say.said: Non si preoccupi, glielo prendo io.
say.en: Don't worry, I'll take it in for you.

steps.title: Come in, take your time
steps.how_to: How to make a polite command sound like a friendly invitation.
steps.intro: Today you'll turn a polite command into a warm invitation, the way people do when they ask you in or tell you to take your time. Two small words do it: pure and prego.

examples.said: Entri pure!
examples.en: Come on in!

examples.said: Faccia pure con calma.
examples.en: Take your time.

examples.said: Prego, si sieda.
examples.en: Please, sit down.

examples.said: Mi dia pure la borsa, gliela tengo io.
examples.en: Go ahead and give me your bag, I'll hold it for you.

steps.notice: Pure after the verb, or prego before it, makes a command sound like an invitation. Here pure means "go ahead," not "also."

ask.said: Un vicino anziano bussa alla tua porta e dice: "Permesso?" Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: An older neighbor knocks on your door and says, "May I come in?" What do you say?

answer.said: Prego, entri pure!
answer.en: Please, come on in!

ask.said: Una signora cerca i soldi e ti chiede scusa. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A woman is looking for her money and apologizes to you. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Faccia pure con calma.
answer.en: Take your time.

ask.said: Una signora anziana ha una borsa pesante. Cosa le offri?
ask.en: An older woman has a heavy bag. What do you offer her?

answer.said: Mi dia pure la borsa, gliela tengo io.
answer.en: Go ahead and give me your bag, I'll hold it for you.

mission.goal: Invite an older neighbor into your home.

say.said: Prego, entri pure!
say.en: Please, come on in!

steps.title: A few, everyone, something
steps.how_to: How to say a few, everyone and something with qualche, ognuno and qualcosa di.
steps.intro: These words help you talk about how many or which ones without counting: a few minutes, everyone, something hot. You'll hear them at counters and in waiting rooms.

examples.said: Aspetti qualche minuto, arrivo subito.
examples.en: Wait a few minutes, I'll be right with you.

examples.said: C'è qualche problema?
examples.en: Is there a problem?

examples.said: Ognuno ha il suo numero: adesso tocca al quarantadue.
examples.en: Everyone has a number, and now it's forty-two's turn.

examples.said: Desidera qualcosa di caldo?
examples.en: Would you like something hot?

steps.notice: Qualche means "a few" or "some" but always takes a singular noun: qualche minuto. Ognuno means "everyone," and qualcosa di plus a describing word means "something" of that kind.

ask.said: Dal medico, di solito quanto aspetti?
ask.en: How long do you usually wait at the doctor's?

answer.said: Di solito aspetto qualche minuto.
answer.en: I usually wait a few minutes.

ask.said: Fa freddo e sei al bar. Cosa vuoi bere?
ask.en: It's cold and you're at the bar. What do you want to drink?

answer.said: Vorrei qualcosa di caldo.
answer.en: I'd like something hot.

ask.said: In sala d'attesa, come sai quando tocca a te?
ask.en: In the waiting room, how do you know when it's your turn?

answer.said: Ognuno ha il suo numero.
answer.en: Everyone has their own number.

mission.goal: Order something hot to drink.

say.said: Vorrei qualcosa di caldo, per favore.
say.en: I'd like something hot, please.

b1-10.title: Work, study and a language course

steps.title: Asking the right question
steps.how_to: How to ask which, how much, how come and how long.
steps.intro: Today you'll ask the questions that come up when you sign up for a course or meet someone new. Each question word asks for something different.

examples.said: Quali sono i Suoi punti di forza?
examples.en: What are your strengths?

examples.said: Da quanto tempo studia l'italiano?
examples.en: How long have you been studying Italian?

examples.said: Come mai proprio in Italia?
examples.en: Why Italy, of all places?

examples.said: Quanto dura il corso e quanto costa?
examples.en: How long is the course, and how much does it cost?

steps.notice: Quali sono asks "what are" when you choose from a set, like strengths. Come mai means "how come," and da quanto tempo asks how long something has been going on.

ask.said: Vuoi sapere il prezzo di un corso. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You want to know the price of a course. What do you ask?

answer.said: Quanto costa il corso?
answer.en: How much does the course cost?

ask.said: Una signora parla molto bene l'inglese. Cosa le chiedi?
ask.en: A woman speaks English very well. What do you ask her?

answer.said: Da quanto tempo studia l'inglese?
answer.en: How long have you been studying English?

ask.said: Un signore americano vive qui da poco. Cosa gli chiedi?
ask.en: An American man has just moved here. What do you ask him?

answer.said: Come mai proprio in Italia?
answer.en: Why Italy, of all places?

mission.goal: At a language school, ask how long the course lasts and what it costs.

say.said: Quanto dura il corso e quanto costa?
say.en: How long is the course, and how much does it cost?

steps.title: How long, then and now
steps.how_to: How to say how long you did something, and how long you've been doing it.
steps.intro: Now you'll say how long you did something in the past and how long you've been doing something now. Italian uses per for the first and da for the second.

examples.said: Ho lavorato per vent'anni come ingegnere.
examples.en: I worked as an engineer for twenty years.

examples.said: Ho lavorato per dieci anni nel turismo.
examples.en: I worked in tourism for ten years.

examples.said: Studio l'italiano da un anno.
examples.en: I've been studying Italian for a year.

examples.said: Vivo in Italia da due anni.
examples.en: I've been living in Italy for two years.

steps.notice: For something that's over, use the past with per: ho lavorato per vent'anni. For something still going on, use the present with da, because it hasn't stopped: studio da un anno.

ask.said: Che lavoro facevi prima?
ask.en: What did you do for work before?

answer.said: Ho lavorato per … anni come …
answer.en: I worked as a … for … years.

ask.said: È tanto che studi l'italiano?
ask.en: Have you been studying Italian long?

answer.said: Studio l'italiano da …
answer.en: I've been studying Italian for …

ask.said: Da quanto tempo vivi in questa città?
ask.en: How long have you lived in this city?

answer.said: Vivo qui da …
answer.en: I've been living here for …

mission.goal: Tell a neighbor how long you've been studying Italian.

say.said: Studio l'italiano da un anno.
say.en: I've been studying Italian for a year.

steps.title: Saying what you do
steps.how_to: How to say what your job is and what field you work in.
steps.intro: Today you'll answer one of the first questions people ask here: what do you do? There are a few ways to say it.

examples.said: E Lei, di cosa si occupa?
examples.en: And what do you do?

examples.said: Sono ingegnere.
examples.en: I'm an engineer.

examples.said: Lavoro come traduttrice.
examples.en: I work as a translator.

examples.said: Mi occupo di marketing.
examples.en: I work in marketing.

steps.notice: Say your job with sono and no word for "a": sono ingegnere. You can also say lavoro come, or mi occupo di for a field.

ask.said: Che lavoro fai?
ask.en: What do you do for a living?

answer.said: Lavoro come …
answer.en: I work as a …

ask.said: In che campo lavori?
ask.en: What field are you in?

answer.said: Mi occupo di …
answer.en: I work in …

ask.said: Che lavoro vorresti fare in Italia?
ask.en: What job would you like to do in Italy?

answer.said: Vorrei lavorare come …
answer.en: I'd like to work as a …

mission.goal: Tell a neighbor what you do for a living.

say.said: Mi occupo di marketing.
say.en: I work in marketing.

steps.title: Writing to an office
steps.how_to: How to open and close a short formal email.
steps.intro: Now you'll learn to start and end a short formal email to a school or an office. You can say it aloud or write it.

examples.said: Gentile dottoressa Rossi,
examples.en: Dear Dr. Rossi,

examples.said: Le scrivo per chiedere informazioni sul corso.
examples.en: I'm writing to ask for information about the course.

examples.said: Cordiali saluti.
examples.en: Best regards,

examples.said: In attesa di una Sua risposta, Le porgo cordiali saluti.
examples.en: I look forward to hearing from you. Best regards,

steps.notice: Open with Gentile plus a title and surname, say why you're writing with Le scrivo per, and close with Cordiali saluti. Gentile works for a man or a woman.
steps.context: Anyone with a degree may be called dottore or dottoressa, so emails to offices open with Gentile, the title and the surname.

ask.said: Scrivi un'email alla segreteria della scuola. Come cominci?
ask.en: You're writing an email to the school office. How do you start?

answer.said: Gentile dottoressa Rossi,
answer.en: Dear Dr. Rossi,

ask.said: Vuoi sapere di più sul corso intensivo. Cosa scrivi nell'email?
ask.en: You want to know more about the intensive course. What do you write in the email?

answer.said: Le scrivo per chiedere informazioni sul corso intensivo.
answer.en: I'm writing to ask for information about the intensive course.

ask.said: Come chiudi un'email formale?
ask.en: How do you end a formal email?

answer.said: Cordiali saluti.
answer.en: Best regards,

mission.goal: Dictate the opening of an email asking about a course.

say.said: Gentile dottoressa Rossi, Le scrivo per chiedere informazioni sul corso.
say.en: Dear Dr. Rossi, I'm writing to ask for information about the course.

steps.title: Glad, sorry or afraid
steps.how_to: How to say how you feel about what someone else does.
steps.intro: Today you'll say how someone else's news makes you feel: glad, sorry or afraid. After these feelings, Italian uses the subjunctive.

examples.said: Sono contenta che tu sia venuto.
examples.en: I'm glad you came.

examples.said: Mi dispiace molto che stia male.
examples.en: I'm so sorry he's not well.

examples.said: Ho paura che non arrivi in tempo.
examples.en: I'm afraid he won't get here in time.

examples.said: Mi fa piacere che ti trovi bene.
examples.en: I'm glad you're settling in well.

steps.notice: After a feeling plus che, the next verb is in the subjunctive, because it's how you feel about something, not a plain fact. For something already done, use sia plus the past: che tu sia venuto.

ask.said: Una tua amica è malata. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend of yours is sick. What do you say to her?

answer.said: Mi dispiace che tu stia male.
answer.en: I'm sorry you're not feeling well.

ask.said: Un amico arriva a casa tua da Milano. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend arrives at your place from Milan. What do you say to him?

answer.said: Sono contento che tu sia venuto!
answer.en: I'm glad you came!

ask.said: Il tuo amico è ancora in viaggio e la cena è pronta. Cosa temi?
ask.en: Your friend is still on the way and dinner is ready. What are you worried about?

answer.said: Ho paura che non arrivi in tempo.
answer.en: I'm afraid he won't get here in time.

mission.goal: Tell a neighbor you're sorry her husband is ill.

say.said: Mi dispiace molto che stia male.
say.en: I'm so sorry he's not well.

steps.title: Glad to see you
steps.how_to: How to say how you feel about something you do yourself.
steps.intro: Now you'll say how you feel about something you yourself do: glad to see someone, sorry you can't come. Here Italian uses di and the plain verb.

examples.said: Sono contento di vederti!
examples.en: I'm so glad to see you!

examples.said: Mi dispiace di non poter venire.
